name: Alhambra, Generalife and Albayzín, Granada
description: Perched on two hills above Granada in southern Spain, the Alhambra was a walled royal city begun in 1238 by the Nasrid emirs, with palaces, gardens and fortress towers. Visitors can wander its intricately carved courtyards, then stroll through the Generalife's terraced gardens, the emirs' country retreat. Across the valley, the Albaycín's whitewashed lanes preserve Moorish-style houses.
